title: Mukdahan to Savannakhet 2026: Indochina Market + Lao Border Plan | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A half-day-block plan for Mukdahan, Thailand: browse the Indochina Market by the Mekong in the morning, then take the bus across Friendship Bridge 2 to old-town Savannakhet, Laos. With bus times, fares, border paperwork, and what's actually open on the Lao side.
keywords: Mukdahan border crossing, Savannakhet, Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge 2, Mukdahan Indochina Market, Laos trip from Mukdahan
h1:
Crossing from Mukdahan
The Indochina Market, then over Bridge 2 to Savannakhet
intro: Mukdahan sits right on the Mekong, and looking across the water you can see Savannakhet in Laos almost within reach. This plan spends the morning walking the Indochina Market along the Mekong on the Thai side, then takes a public bus across the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge 2 to explore Savannakhet's old town from midday into the evening. It's an easy cross-border trip you can pull off in just a couple of days. We've laid it out in half-day blocks so you can see where to be and when, and we spell out the border paperwork and bus timing clearly from the start.

blocks.html: Before we get into the plan, it helps to know that this crossing has two checkpoints in practice: the Mukdahan border checkpoint on the Thai side at the foot of the bridge, and the Savannakhet checkpoint on the Lao side. The public bus shuttles between these two checkpoints across the second Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge, a total distance of about 17 km. The actual ride takes around an hour once you factor in document checks on both sides, and the fare is roughly 45 THB per trip. What eats the most time isn't the distance, it's the passport queue. So this plan has you leave the Thai side mid-morning rather than rushing across before dawn.

blocks.text: Paperwork and what to know before you cross

blocks.html: Paperwork is where people get confused most often, so let's keep it clear. Foreign visitors typically cross into Savannakhet on a passport, and many nationalities can enter Laos visa-free or on a visa on arrival, which lets you travel anywhere in the country. There's also a temporary Border Pass option available to Thai citizens (issued at the Mueang Mukdahan district office or at service points by the checkpoint, using only a Thai ID card), but it only allows travel within Savannakhet province and has a limited number of days. If you're only doing a day trip into Savannakhet town, a Border Pass is enough; but if you want to stay overnight or venture further, a passport is far more flexible.

items: Money — the Lao side takes both kip and baht; many shops in town accept THB directly, though the rate may not be great. Carry some kip for the market and songthaew rides.
Checkpoint fees — the Lao side often collects a small entry/exit fee in cash, especially outside office hours and on holidays. Keep small notes handy.

Checkpoint hours — the border is open from morning into the evening, but going early and returning before dusk is the safest bet for catching a bus. Don't plan your return for early evening, as bus frequency thins out.
SIM/data — your Thai signal cuts out once you cross the bridge. Turn on roaming or buy a Lao SIM at a shop in Savannakhet town if you need data for a longer stay.
Time in Laos — same as Thailand, no need to adjust your watch.

blocks.title: About the cross-border bus
blocks.html: The Mukdahan-Savannakhet public bus run by Thailand's Transport Co. (BKS) departs from Mukdahan Bus Terminal. Check schedules and book ahead on the E-Ticket app, at transport.co.th, or by calling 1490. If you're driving your own car, you'll need paperwork to take the vehicle out of the country, which is more of a hassle. For a simple sightseeing trip, the easiest move is to park on the Thai side and take the bus across.

blocks.text: Block 1 · Morning: Walk the Indochina Market by the Mekong

blocks.html: The Mukdahan Indochina Market stretches along Samran Chai Khong Road, right beside the Mekong in the town center. It's one of the largest souvenir markets in Isan, open daily from around 8am. Goods range from imports out of China, Vietnam, and Laos to local Mukdahan silk and crafts. Mornings are more pleasant to walk, since the sun isn't harsh yet and the stalls are fully stocked. Use this block to shop, grab a snack, and take in the Mekong views across to Savannakhet on the far bank.

blocks.label: Morning Block
blocks.title: Indochina Market + the Mekong in Mukdahan

items.activity: Start at the Indochina Market on Samran Chai Khong Road
items.note: Browse the souvenir, clothing, and import zones. Polite bargaining is fine.

items.activity: Breakfast bites at the edge of the market
items.note: Grab coffee, sweets, and a snack to line your stomach before crossing, in case the checkpoint queue runs long.

items.activity: Take photos along the Mekong embankment, looking across to Savannakhet
items.note: The riverside viewpoint is a short walk on from the market; you can see Bridge 2 spanning the water.

items.activity: Wrap up and head to Mukdahan Bus Terminal
items.note: Leave time to buy your cross-border bus ticket and join the checkpoint queue.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: In recent years part of the Indochina Market has been closed for renovation, and the stalls aren't as lively as in its heyday. Some shops close on weekdays. If you want the full buzz, aim for a weekend, but if you're hoping for the cheap, unusual finds of the old days, you may have to temper your expectations a little.

blocks.text: Block 2 · Late morning to midday: Cross Friendship Bridge 2

blocks.html: This is the heart of the plan. From Mukdahan Bus Terminal you board the public bus, which stops at the Mukdahan border checkpoint so you can get your Thai exit stamp, then you reboard and the bus crosses Friendship Bridge 2 over the Mekong to the Savannakhet checkpoint where you handle Lao entry. After that the bus carries you into Savannakhet town. The bridge itself is over 1.6 km long; the view from the middle is lovely, but you can't get off to take photos, you have to stay on the bus. If the queues aren't long, the whole process takes about an hour.

items.activity: Board the bus at Mukdahan Bus Terminal
items.note: Fare is roughly 45 THB per trip. Keep your ticket for the return.

items.activity: Stop at Mukdahan checkpoint, get your Thai exit stamp
items.note: Have your passport or Border Pass ready and fill in the forms at the counter.

items.activity: Cross Friendship Bridge 2 on the bus
items.note: The Mekong view from the middle of the bridge is great here, but only shoot from inside the bus.

items.activity: Reach the Savannakhet checkpoint, handle Lao entry
items.note: There may be a small fee in cash, so keep small notes handy.
Take a connecting ride or tuk-tuk into the riverside old town.

blocks.text: Block 3 · Afternoon: Walk Savannakhet's old town

blocks.html: Savannakhet's old town has a charm unlike other Lao tourist towns: quiet, slow, and full of French colonial shophouses still standing. The hub is the central town square, where St. Teresa's Church, an old Catholic church, stands out as the landmark. Around it are faded-paint old buildings, some now open as cafes and guesthouses. This afternoon block is made for unhurried wandering, stopping to take photos and sitting over a coffee while you watch the town go by.

items.name: Central town square + St. Teresa's Church
items.blurb: The middle of the old town, ringed by French-era buildings. The old Catholic church is the main photo spot, and the whole quarter is walkable.

items.name: Savannakhet Dinosaur Museum
items.blurb: Holds dinosaur fossils dug up in the province. Open mornings until around 11:30am, so if you want to go in, plan it as a morning block on a second day.

items.name: Savan Xai Market (Singapore Market)
items.blurb: A big central market on Sisavangvong Road with food and goods of all kinds. Locals call it the Singapore Market.

items.name: The Mekong on the Savannakhet side
items.blurb: A riverside walk where you look back across to Mukdahan. Breezy in the late afternoon, a nice spot to rest before heading back.

items.note: Try khao piak sen (rice noodle soup), pho, or Lao coffee. Plenty of spots around the square.

items.activity: Visit St. Teresa's Church and the old buildings around the square
items.note: Easy strolling and photos; this quarter has little traffic, so you can walk the whole block.

items.activity: Drop by Savan Xai Market, or settle into a cafe in an old building
items.note: Pick up Lao souvenirs like coffee, Beerlao, and sweets.

items.activity: Walk the Mekong on the Lao side, looking back toward Mukdahan
items.note: A photo stop to close out the trip before heading back to the checkpoint.

items.activity: Return to the Savannakhet checkpoint and catch the bus back across
items.note: Don't leave it too late into the evening; buses run less often as it gets dark.

blocks.title: If you have more than one day
blocks.html: If you want to pay respects at That Ing Hang Stupa, said to be a twin of Phra That Phanom, allow extra time, since it's outside town. It works best as a morning block on a second day before you cross back to Mukdahan in the afternoon. If you're on a Border Pass doing a single day trip, just focus on the old town in the city center.

blocks.text: Block 4 · Evening: Back to Mukdahan, close the trip by the Mekong

blocks.html: The return mirrors the way out, just with the checkpoints reversed: stop at the Savannakhet checkpoint for your Lao exit stamp, cross the bridge back, then stop at the Mukdahan checkpoint to re-enter Thailand. You'll reach the Thai side around early evening, perfect timing for dinner by the Mekong. The Samran Chai Khong Road area has restaurants and spots to sit and watch the sun set over the river, a fitting way to wrap up a cross-border trip before heading back to your accommodation in Mukdahan town.

items: Dinner by the Mekong in Mukdahan — Mekong river fish and Isan food along Samran Chai Khong Road, with a sunset view.
Ho Kaeo Mukdahan tower — if you still have energy, take in the town and Mekong views from up high (better saved for the next day).
Keep your bus ticket and checkpoint documents — double-check that your entry and exit stamps are correct for both countries.

faq.q: Do I need a passport to cross to Savannakhet, or is an ID card enough?
faq.a: Both can work. On a passport, most visitors enter Laos visa-free or with a visa on arrival and can travel anywhere in the country. Thai citizens can instead get a temporary Border Pass at the Mueang Mukdahan district office using a Thai ID card, but it only allows travel within Savannakhet province and has a limited number of days. For a day trip into town, a Border Pass is enough.

faq.q: Where do I catch the Mukdahan-Savannakhet bus, and what's the fare?
faq.a: Take the Transport Co. (BKS) public bus from Mukdahan Bus Terminal. The fare is roughly 45 THB per trip over a distance of about 17 km, and the ride takes around an hour once you include document checks at both checkpoints. Check schedules and book on the E-Ticket app, at transport.co.th, or by calling 1490.

faq.q: Can I walk across Friendship Bridge 2 myself?
faq.a: No. The second Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge doesn't allow walking or cycling across; you have to take the public bus, a private car, or a hired vehicle. The view from the middle is lovely, but you can only shoot it from inside the vehicle.

faq.q: Can I do Savannakhet as a day trip, leaving in the morning and returning in the evening?
faq.a: Yes. If you leave the Thai side mid-morning and return before early evening, you'll have plenty of time to walk the old town and market. But if you also want to visit That Ing Hang Stupa outside town, plan to stay one night and bring a passport.

faq.q: Can I use Thai baht on the Lao side?
faq.a: In many places, yes. Plenty of shops in town and at the market accept baht directly, though the rate may not be great. We'd suggest carrying some kip for the market and songthaew rides, and keeping small cash notes for the Lao-side checkpoint fees.
